briefing_title_en: Daily Briefing, Oct. 26, 2026: AI Governance, Brazil Election and China Plenum
briefing_summary_en: In eight sections: Kimi K3.1 Pro launched without open weights, promised by Nov. 4; OpenAI says it will stop training on the live internet citing risks; papers focus on agent safety and jailbreaking. Vercel adds budgets, feedback, cache and managed Stripe keys. Science reports include five silicon qubits, Bennu samples, three black holes and an exomoon candidate. Globally, Lula wins Brazil’s fourth term and Bolsonaro’s camp seeks annulment; Israel closes West Bank crossings on election day; storms cut power to about 150,000 homes. China’s 20th CPC Central Committee Fifth Plenum opens, and the water ministry sets ecological flow targets for 382 cross-provincial rivers and lakes. Markets watch copper and AI stocks, China’s “national team” ETF inflows and Indian small-cap margin pressure. Opinion covers software ambition and open-weight models.

sections.briefing_title_en: China Watch: CPC plenum opens as water, livelihood and public safety issues advance
sections.briefing_summary_en: The Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee opened in Beijing, with Xi Jinping delivering a work report and explaining a draft decision on full and rigorous Party governance. The water ministry set ecological flow targets for 382 cross-provincial rivers and lakes, while more than 90% of prefecture-level and above cities are advancing 15-minute community life circles. The Jianghan water diversion project is using nine machines simultaneously for tunnel construction; geological hazard checks were completed within 50 km of the Bachen earthquake epicenter; the meteorological administration refuted claims of a cyclone 'hitting the Himalayas'; and reports examined mandatory travel insurance and rescue pressures from inexperienced hikers entering wild mountains.
